root_motivation: grand-loop-billing (v0.14.0) gave mcphost plans, quotas, checkout, and the webhook that flips a tenant to `pro`. What it does not do is bill usage: the live Stripe account has a meter (`mcphost_tool_calls`) and a graduated metered price (`price_1UCZQRIPqmv0aTON9zg3eZ38`, zero to 50,000 then $0.001 per call) that nothing feeds. Checkout creates a subscription on the base price alone, the webhook discards the session's `customer` id, and no code reads the `calls` table for billing. A pro tenant at 10 million calls a month pays $19. The catalog ids live in `~/.config/mcphost/stripe-objects.json`; the price is attached to the same product checkout already sells.
user_persona: An AI agent connecting to mcphost for the first time over streamable HTTP with default client configuration (Claude Agent SDK / Claude Code), which must be able to read a well-formed tool list before it can do anything else; secondarily the operator who probes the endpoint after a redeploy.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given migration 0007 on a v0.14.0 data dir, When `mcphost serve` starts, Then existing tenants load with null `stripe_customer_id` and the full prior suite passes unchanged.
Given a signed `checkout.session.completed` with a `customer` id, When the webhook processes it, Then the tenant row stores that id and the upgrade behavior of AC6 (grand-loop-billing) is unchanged.

Given `metered_price_id` configured and a fake billing client, When `billing.checkout` runs, Then the fake receives two line items, base with quantity 1 and metered without quantity; and Given no `metered_price_id`, Then it receives exactly the single-price call shape from v0.14.0.

Given 250 ok pro calls, 40 ok free calls, and 10 failed pro calls above the high-water mark, When `billing emit-meter` runs against the fake, Then the fake receives events summing to 250 for the pro tenant only, `meter_state.last_call_id` is the newest pro ok call id, and one ledger row records the batch span.

Given a run that crashes after the POST but before the state write (test injects the fault), When `emit-meter` reruns, Then the resent batch carries identical `identifier` values and the ledger marks it a replay.
Given the fake returns 500, When `emit-meter` runs, Then it exits non-zero, `meter_state` is unmoved, and no ledger row is written.
Given 120 pending pro tenants' batches, When one run executes, Then no request carries more than 100 events and all pending spans are covered across requests.
Given metering configured and 30 unemitted pro ok calls, When `/healthz` is read, Then `meter_lag` is 30; and Given metering unconfigured, Then the key is absent.
Given `deploy/mcphost-emit-meter.timer`, When `systemd-analyze verify` runs on both unit files, Then it exits clean, and the README operator section documents installation.
Given the full suite and `autobuilder gate --project .` at the landed HEAD, When they run, Then every previously passing test passes and the gate reports pass=25 block=0.
Given three ledgered batches, When an admin calls `admin.meter_status`, Then it reports last batch span, current lag, and per-tenant emitted counts for the month.
Given a configured key and a pro tenant, When `billing.status` runs with the fake returning an accepted-usage total, Then the response includes that total labeled as Stripe-reported.
acceptance_criteria.test: no unit test file; live smoke — mcphost serve + synthorg consume --preflight <url>, recorded as target/autobuilder/ac12-preflight-smoke.json

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a fresh data dir with no `plans.toml`, When mcphost starts, Then `billing.plans` reports free with `tools_max` 50 and price 0, and pro with price 19 and a description naming 50,000 included monthly calls.

scope: Derive the advertised MCP-Protocol-Version from rmcp::model::ProtocolVersion::LATEST instead of a string literal.
Emit ttlMs and cacheScope on every tools/list response in all four authentication states, set in one place all branches flow through.
Correct the protocol_version_and_log doc comment to match the layer's actual router-wide scope.
non_goals: Adding real support for protocol 2026-07-28 (SEP-2243 Mcp-Method / Mcp-Param-* headers and per-request _meta).
The tenant-key hand-off, which is PRD-mcphost-session-key and depends on this PRD.
Any consumer-facing feature candidate; no measured baseline exists to rank one against.
Changes to synthorg, whose preflight asserts only that the protocol header is present, not its value.

additional.no_panic_in_src: BAD_RUST denies unwrap/expect/panic in src/; HeaderValue::from_str is fallible and must be handled without panicking.
additional.single_application_point: Requirement 5: the cache fields must be applied once for all Auth branches, not chained per branch.
additional.no_existing_test_weakened: AC15: no pre-existing test may be deleted, ignored, or weakened.
additional.unsafe_scope: unsafe is confined to src/sandbox.rs pre_exec_setup, where only async-signal-safe libc calls run between fork and exec; this PRD adds none.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can no agent use the deployed mcphost endpoint?
five_whys_trace.a: Its client connects and initializes successfully but sees an empty tool list, so there is nothing to call.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the tool list empty for that client?
five_whys_trace.a: The client's tools/list request is refused before mcphost's handler runs, and the error body it parses has no ttlMs or cacheScope, so it reports the result invalid and shows zero tools.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the request refused, and why are those fields missing?
five_whys_trace.a: The client sends MCP-Protocol-Version 2026-07-28, which trips rmcp's SEP-2243 validators demanding an Mcp-Method header and per-request _meta; and list_tools sets the cache fields only on the Auth::Tenant branch, so the anonymous branch every new agent hits omits them.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the client send 2026-07-28 when rmcp negotiates 2025-11-25?
five_whys_trace.a: Because mcphost's own middleware stamps a hardcoded 2026-07-28 onto every response including initialize, and rmcp never writes that response header itself, so mcphost is the sole source of an advertisement it cannot honour.

five_whys_trace.q: Why was the constant hardcoded to a version the server cannot serve?
five_whys_trace.a: The vision's Lineage section asserted that rmcp 3.2.0 serves 2026-07-28 statelessly by default; in fact ProtocolVersion::LATEST is 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 is only the SEP-2243 threshold. The literal encoded a mistaken belief, and the tests that would have caught it only ever exercised the authenticated branch.

ambiguities_resolved.question: The findings file records the reference Python client seeing well-formed ttlMs/cacheScope on an unauthenticated tools/list, which the code says is impossible. Which is right?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Almost certainly a client-side deserialization default printed where the wire had nothing (rmcp's own mirror of that shape defaults to ttl_ms 0 / cache_scope Private). Settled by a test rather than an argument: AC2 asserts on the serialized wire JSON, not a deserialized model.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Requirement 9 offers two ways to fix the middleware doc/scope mismatch: re-scope the layer to /mcp, or correct the comment to say it is router-wide. Which?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Correct the comment. It is the smaller behavioural change, and an unauthenticated health endpoint carrying an accurate protocol-version header is harmless.
